title: Excitable chemotactic agents (new class excitable-chemotaxis, Dictyostelium-like relay): from a uniform random gas, 6000 FitzHugh-Nagumo agents that relay a diffusing signal and climb its gradient only while excited collapse into ~100 discrete aggregates that fire as units and coarsen to 7-11 by t=1000; no persistent splits and little motion (2 seeds)
summary: world.py: agents carry a FitzHugh-Nagumo excitable state, fire spontaneously at a low rate, secrete a diffusing, decaying signal while excited (saturating response), and move up its gradient only while excited (adaptation), with soft pair repulsion; nothing marks an individual. From uniform random positions (seeds 0-1, T=1000) the gas breaks into ~110 aggregates by t~80, which fire collectively (pink in the sheet: excited fraction), contract while firing, relax while refractory, and merge into 7-11 large round aggregates (occupancy 0.17); labkit counts 154-176 splits but 0-1 persistent ones (merge/split 1.6) and max 1.3-1.5 body lengths of motion. Controls on seed 0: with chemotaxis off (v0=0) the uniform gas carries large relay waves but never aggregates; with secretion off (ks=0) nothing happens, so aggregation needs relay and chemotaxis together.
